This course should be given in the first year, second semester, as MBG 102. Only 30-40 % was about biochemistry, and other parts were more about experimental techniques. Students should know what is cloning, western blot, and other things in their first year, not in their third year. Students should know the chemistry of biomolecules in the first place. But this course almost does not teach the chemistry of biomolecules. 3rd-year MBG students cannot even draw hydrogen bonds between nucleotides. But they know their names for sure. Students should be able to derive equations of enzyme kinetics, not memorize formulas. However, analyzing graphs was a good practice. Students should know the structure of every amino acid and understand their properties, which was achieved partially in this course. Overall, the course gives very important concepts of biochemistry and helps students reach the average level of interpreting biochemistry. The course should be simplified and presented more on a chemical basis. Experimental techniques were good to learn, but many old methods and concepts are not famous these days and can be learned easily from the internet if it becomes necessary. Lab were also useful, but overburning students with excessive work, many waiting hours, and writing a bunch of lab reports with strict deadlines as if they would be immediately checked. So far, I only know my grade for the first lab report. Then, what is the purpose of stressing students and giving short deadlines if they don't check it on time? Close to the end, I just started using AI to write a lab report instead of wasting time. Lab reports took up half of my free time. Cloning, LDH, titration, and western blot were very good practices. The course is good, but can be organized better.
